content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I've successfully configured my system for remote access to my [product_name] after two hours of troubleshooting router settings with [company_name] support. Currently, the only way I can connect to my [product_name] is by entering my WAN address in the app's address bar, and on the router ([product_name] model) assigning the DMZ to the IP address of the [product_name]. Is this correct? We plan to access several [product_name] modules on-site, but I'm unsure if using DMZ is suitable since it only covers one [product_name]. We have a strict deadline in two weeks and are running short on time. Thanks in advance.

Hello, Have you considered using a Dynamic DNS service? These are commonly used for most internet connectivity solutions. They allow you to connect using a domain name rather than just an IP address. You can visit providers like no-IP.com or dyndns.org, among others. Essentially, your router should support a DynDNS client; once set up, you choose a domain name that points to your [product_name] and the current IP address. The DynDNS server maintains the mapping between your domain name and IP address. If your ISP changes your router's IP (usually daily), the router with DynDNS updates the server with the new address. With this solution, frequent IP address changes by your ISP won’t affect remote connectivity to your [product_name]. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: The user requires reliable remote access to several [product_name] modules, but the current DMZ-based method only supports connectivity to a single device. This limits scalability and usability for accessing multiple modules on-site. Suggestions involving Dynamic DNS services may offer alternative solutions, but do not directly address simultaneous multi-device access.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is seeking a simple and scalable method to remotely access multiple [product_name] modules without having to assign the DMZ to only one device.
